task_text: Moving ramp relay: An orange ball rests in the left Panda's cup, and the right Panda holds a straight channel that is open at both ends. The left arm must pass the ball into the inlet part of the channel. The ball must then leave the channel by its outlet end and be caught again in free flight by the left cup. The relay is then repeated with the channel held at a clearly different orientation from the first time. After the second catch, the left cup must deliver the ball into a fixed basin, where it must come to rest. Phases, in order: first_channel_entry: The ball touches the channel (any part of panda-1's tool) while two things hold. Its centre is more than 0.045 m from the channel centre on the inlet side (channel-frame x < -0.045). And at that moment it does not touch the cup. The channel's pose (position and orientation) at that moment is recorded.; first_moving_exit: The ball's centre is more than 0.13 m from the channel centre on the outlet side (channel-frame x > 0.13, i.e. within 1 cm of the outlet end or past it; y and z are not bounded), while the ball does not touch the channel. At that moment the world speed of the channel's outlet tip must be at least `outlet_min_speed`, which is 0 at this instance.; first_catch: The ball enters the left cup from above and is retained. The entry: after touching nothing for at least 0.025 s, the ball's centre passes downward through the plane 0.073 m above the cup floor (wall height 0.055 m + radius 0.018 m, in the cup's frame). At that crossing the centre must be within 0.052 m (`tool_half` - radius) of the cup centre along both cup x and cup y. From then on the ball must stay contained in the cup for 0.18 s without interruption. Contained in the cup means all of the following, in the cup's frame: |x| and |y| of the ball centre below 0.0619 m (`tool_half` - 0.45 x radius); height above the cup floor between 0.014 m and 0.0528 m; in contact with the cup within the last 25 ms; moving at less than 0.09 m/s relative to the cup (including the cup's rotation). The free-flight time counts only from the start of this phase.; second_channel_entry: As in first_channel_entry, the ball touches the channel at channel-frame x < -0.045 while not touching the cup. In addition, the channel's orientation must differ by at least 0.30 rad (about 17.2 deg) from the orientation recorded at the first entry, i.e. |q . q_first| <= cos 0.15 for the unit quaternions. A touch while the orientation is too close to the first one does not count.; second_moving_exit: As in first_moving_exit: the ball's centre is at channel-frame x > 0.13 while the ball does not touch the channel, and the outlet tip moves at least `outlet_min_speed` (0 here).; second_catch_and_delivery: First the ball is caught again in the left cup exactly as in first_catch. That is: an entry after at least 0.025 s of free flight (counted from the start of this phase) through the plane 0.073 m above the cup floor within 0.052 m of the centre on both axes, then contained in the cup for 0.18 s without interruption. After that catch, the ball must be contained in the basin and not touch the cup, for 0.7 s without interruption. Contained in the basin means all of the following, in the basin's frame (origin at the centre of its floor's top surface, axes = world axes): |x| and |y| of the ball centre below 0.0669 m (0.075 - 0.45 x radius); height above the basin floor between 0.014 m and 0.0578 m; in contact with the basin within the last 25 ms; speed below 0.09 m/s. This completes the task. Goal geometry: All phase geometry is relative to the channel, the cup and the basin.
episode: one episode, no reset: it ends at the first control step where the task has succeeded (every phase in order) or failed (a failure event, a forbidden contact, a safety-limit violation, an object out of bounds, or the task's horizon of 25 s of simulated time, 2500 control steps), when your time is up, or on a simulator error; the simulated clock advances only with the control steps you run
